root_causes.evidence: Reconciliation session held a write lock on accounts for 13 s+, ledger write_errors 107 and payments error rate 42%; after release_lock write errors went to 0 and payments errors to 0.
Clearing was down (exit code 15, no errors in its logs) and the queue was building with the head item at 0 attempts; after restart it processed 12.9/s and the queue drained to 1.

actions.reason: Reconciliation holds a write lock on the ledger, causing payment write errors; release it first, then look at clearing which is down.

sbar.situation: Payments have recovered and recovery was confirmed on two clean looks in a row, the last at 38 s. Payments error rate is 0, p95 is at baseline, and the probe journey passes end to end.
sbar.background: A reconciliation session held a write lock on the accounts table in the ledger for over 13 s, causing 107 ledger write errors and a 42% payments error rate. At the same time clearing was down (exit code 15, no errors in its logs) and its queue was building, with the head item at 0 attempts.
sbar.assessment: The incident commander itself ended the reconciliation session holding the ledger lock, and ledger write errors and payments errors dropped to 0 (confidence 0.9). It also restarted clearing itself, which then processed 12.9 items/s and drained the queue to 1 (confidence 0.8). The operator restart of screening-standby was benign.
sbar.recommendation: Find out why reconciliation held a long write lock on accounts and why clearing exited with code 15, and prevent both from recurring. Ledger integrity is clean with no unbalanced or duplicate payments, so the operations team has no money or data effects to review.
